tone_and_style.principle: Be direct and technical, not conversational
Focus on actions taken and results achieved
Apply type-aware terminology consistently: use "fix" for bug reports, and "implement" or "add" for feature requests and tasks across all questions, status updates, diff reviews, and summaries

when_to_ask_questions.scenario: MANDATORY GATE #1: Reviewing drafted public issue (title, proposed label, and markdown body, confirming no internal acceptance criteria are included)
Deciding whether to link related issues, close as duplicate, or override
MANDATORY GATE #2: Asking user whether to attempt work on a new feature branch using type-appropriate phrasing (e.g., attempt fix vs implement feature)
MANDATORY GATE #3: Presenting diff and test results and asking user whether to commit, push, and open PR
MANDATORY MANUAL CLOSURE GATE: Presenting drafted manual closure proposal (reason: not planned / duplicate, label changes, and explanatory closing comment) before executing update_issue

MANDATORY BLANKET DESTRUCTIVE ACTION GATE: Requesting explicit confirmation for specific terminal/destructive actions (e.g., deleting branches, deleting comments, closing issues) even when prompted with broad user requests
Prompting for assignee when lazy identity resolution yields no matching account or missing local info
Offering PR merge directly at Phase 6 without pre-evaluation
